text:
mira: Quick Q — customer flagged telemetry headers. They're seeing inconsistent User-Agent strings from our SDKs across lambdas. Example: some requests show `Redwood-Python/0.7.0`, others just `python-requests/2.28`. Any known causes?

sujay: Are those streaming requests or regular HTTP calls? Lambdas + streaming + connection reuse can cause UA to be set only on the initial handshake for some runtimes.

alex: It's streaming. Repro'd with the JS streaming helper. UA appears on the initial handshake only. snippet: `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY }); client.chat.stream(...)`

mira: Also the customer wants to completely opt out of client metrics; I tried `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0` but `x-rw-client-metrics` still appears on requests.

kevin: Heads up — env var names changed across releases. The current stable uses `REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=off`. `REDWOOD_TELEMETRY` controls the in-client telemetry pipeline (events upload), not header injection. We'll add a compatibility note.

sujay: On trace propagation: we propagate `traceparent`/W3C and `tracestate` where present. Note: internal retries do not preserve the original trace by default (we create a new trace for each attempt) to avoid making a failed attempt appear as a successful span in APM.

alex: Customer wants a single trace across retries. Can we expose an opt-in? e.g., `preserve_trace_on_retries: true`?

kevin: We discussed this last quarter — opt-in is fine. We implemented flags in Go/TS/Python but default false. Security/observability teams wanted opt-in so failures remain distinct unless the app explicitly folds attempts together.

mira: How do you disable header injection entirely (UA, `x-rw-client-metrics`, and trace headers)? Policy requires zero telemetry headers for some regulated customers.

sujay: Use config knobs per SDK: JS: `new Redwood({ apiKey, telemetry: { enabled: false, injectHeaders: false }})`
Python: `Client(api_key, telemetry={'enabled': False, 'inject_headers': False})`
Go: `opts := redwood.DefaultOptions(); opts.Telemetry.InjectHeaders = false`

alex: Note: older SDK versions (<=0.6.x) have different env names — `RW_METRICS=0` was the old toggle. Add a migration note.

kevin: Streaming quirk: some proxies drop custom headers during HTTP/2 connection upgrades or when a stream splits frames. We've seen `traceparent` disappear when using certain edge proxies. Workaround: attach critical headers on the initial request and fall back to query param propagation (e.g., `?traceparent=...`) if your infra trusts that pattern. Document the security tradeoffs.

mira: Sounds good. I'll add examples for JS/Python/Go and show the env-var compatibility matrix.

alex: Also mention that connection reuse can make per-request UA updates unreliable in some runtimes — recommend SDK expose `per_request_ua: true` when customers need strict UA telemetry.

sujay: For retries + tracing, test cases: we should add an integration that forces a transient 502 and asserts either (a) trace preserved across attempts when flag is set, or (b) different traces when flag unset.

kevin: I can add an httptest harness to eng-runtime tests to simulate header-stripping proxies and flaky backends.

mira: I'll draft the docs PR and include code snippets + compat table + how-to for complete opt-out. Will ping @kevin and @sujay for review.

devx-bot: Created DOC-432 "telemetry header opt-out and trace/retry guidance" and assigned to mira.

mira: Thanks :thumbsup: — will follow up with the PR link shortly.

alex: One last gotcha: serverless cold starts sometimes show the same trace id across requests if an instrumentation lib caches a header. Add a note to clear cached headers on new request contexts.

sujay: Good call. Add a short snippet for clearing cached trace state in Node and Python.

kevin: I'll review the PR and add the test harness.

mira: Awesome, appreciate the quick help.
